paragraphs.text: Having denounced woe to wicked of all sorts, the prophet here threateneth wicked princes in particular, as the chief causes of God’s judgments by their misgovernment. Periculosissimum prophetae factum, et cui seditionis dica scribi poterat! {a} This was boldly done of the prophet, and there wanted not those doubtless that would say it was sedition. Luther, for like cause, was called the trumpet of rebellion; sc., for declaring against the Pope’s decrees and decretals, though never so unrighteous and vexatious; not much short of that made by Nero, Whosoever confesseth himself a Christian - so a Protestant - let him, without further defence of himself, be put to death as a convicted enemy of mankind!
paragraphs.anchor: Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees.

paragraphs.text: Or, And to the writers that write grievous things - viz., the public notaries, registrars, and other under officers; such as were those Persian scribes and posts, {Est 3:12-13} who should, in such a case, have obeyed God rather than men.
paragraphs.anchor: And that write grievousness.

paragraphs.text: {a} Scultet.
To put them beside their right, because indigent, and overweighed by the wealthy ones: Quorum aureae literae apud tales iudices possunt omnia.
paragraphs.anchor: To turn away the needy from judgment.

paragraphs.text: Heb., To tear it away by force.
paragraphs.anchor: And to take away the right.

paragraphs.text: Rob the spittle, as we used to say. Unrighteous ruledom is but robbery with authority. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And that they may rob the fatherless.

paragraphs.text: {a} Iudex iniustus latro cum privilegio est. - Columel., lib. i.
That is, of vastation by the Assyrians.
paragraphs.anchor: And what will ye do in the day of visitation.

paragraphs.text: Who have denied help to the poor that fled unto you; but sped no better than the sheep that flee to the bush for defence in weather, where he is sure to lose part of his fleece.
paragraphs.anchor: To whom will ye flee for help.

paragraphs.text: Where will ye betrust or bestow your wealth, power, and worldly pomp, purchased by you at too dear a rate? who paid your honesty to get it - O magno emptas, et parum proficuas divitias! - and must now lose not it only, but your liberties and lives also, in the next verse.
paragraphs.anchor: And where will ye leave your glory?

paragraphs.text: i.e., Without any fault of mine. {Hos 13:9} Or, as some render it, Ne corruat inter vinctos, et inter occisos cadant; that it, your glory, should not bow down under the prisoners, and they fall under the slain; i.e., that ye be not some of you captivated, and others slain by the enemy. And yet behold a worse matter.
paragraphs.anchor: Without me they shall bow down under the prisoners

paragraphs.text: Endless torments will follow, unless ye prevent them by repentance, and all your present sufferings are nothing else but a typical hell. {a} Ecce quot mala a contemptu Dei proveniunt.
paragraphs.anchor: For all this his anger is not turned away.

paragraphs.text: {a} Hac oratione vir sanctus impios crueatat, et vulaerat. - Osor.

Or, Woe to the Assyrian; or, Heu Assur, Alas, the Assyrian! q.d., Alas, that I am forced by this sharp and iron rod to correct my people, whom I have bred so choicely! Dolentis vocem assumit Deus, saith Oecolampadius.
paragraphs.anchor: O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger.

paragraphs.text: Or, My rod of anger. A rod of anger to beat the little ones, and a staff of indignation to bastinado the bigger and more stubborn. So Nebuchadnezzar is called the "hammer of the whole earth." {Jer 50:23} Tamerlane called himself, The wrath of God, and the desolation of the world, {a} Attilas styled himself, King of Huns, Medes, Goths, Dacians; "The terror of the world, and God’s scourge." The wicked are God’s rod, said that martyr, whom, when he hath worn to the stump, he will cast into the fire. {b}
paragraphs.anchor: The rod of mine anger.

paragraphs.text: {a} Ira Dei ego sum, et orbis vastitas.
{b} Acts and Mon., fol. 1544.

I will send him … I will give him a charge.] Non patefacta quidem voluntate, sed arcana providentia, I will stir him up by a secret providence, which, being nothing else but the carrying on of the divine decree, is that helm that turneth about the whole ship of the universe.

Pretenders only to religion, {see Isa 9:17} qui toti ex hypocrisi sunt conflati, such as are wholly made up of hypocrisy: God was near in their mouth, and far from their reins. {Jer 12:2} Nemo tam prope proculque Deo. {Mat 15:8} Hot meteors they are. saith one, shooting, yet showing like stars; shaming goodness by seeming good; Virtutis stragulam pudefaciunt, as Diogenes said to Antipater, who, being vicious, wore a white cloak, the ensign of innocence. These are little better than devils wrapped up in Samuel’s mantle; odious therefore to God, whom they would cozen of heaven, if they could tell how.
paragraphs.anchor: Against an hypocritical nation.

paragraphs.text: Who are therefore the worse, and shall fare the worse, because they ought to have been better. Indignation and wrath shall he upon the Jew first, because of his privileges, and then upon the Gentile. {Rom 2:9}
paragraphs.anchor: And against the people of my wrath.

paragraphs.text: As had been foretold in Maher-shalal-hash-baz’s name. {Isa 8:1}
paragraphs.anchor: To take the spoil, and to take the prey.

paragraphs.text: To make mortar of them, as we use to say: Gens simulatrix tota terrena, Is trodden under foot as unsavoury salt, which is not good enough for the dunghill.
paragraphs.anchor: And to tread them down like mire in the streets.

paragraphs.text: He is otherwise minded and affected than I am, and doeth my will merely beside and against his own will. As in applying of leeches the physician seeketh the health of his patient, the leech only the filling of his gorge, so is it when God turneth loose a bloody enemy upon his people; he hath excellent ends, which they think not on.
paragraphs.anchor: Howbeit he meaneth not so.

paragraphs.text: This was to exceed his commission, which was only to "take the spoil, and to take the prey," {Isa 10:6} not to cut off nations, and to make havoc of all. How much better our King Edward the Confessor, who, when his captains promised for his sake they would not leave one Dane alive, thought it better to lead a private and unbloody life than to be a king by such bloody butcheries. {a} Of Charles V, emperor, we read, that when Antonius Leva, and other of his chief commanders, commended Alexander the Great and Julius Caesar for their great exploits in overrunning and destroying nations not a few, to their great renown; and, on the other side, complained that Charles made not the like use of his power and victories as he might and ought to do for such a purpose, he gravely replied, that Alexander and Julius had, in waging wars, nothing else to aim at besides honour and glory, but that Christian princes were in all their enterprises to mind the glory of God and the salvation of their own souls. {b}
paragraphs.anchor: But it is in his heart to destroy and cut off.

paragraphs.text: {a} Camd. Rem., p. 214.
{b} Parei Hist. Prof. Med., p. 895.
Sennacherib saith. See Isa 36:9; Isa 36:15; Isa 36:18; Isa 36:20; Isa 37:10; Isa 37:13; Isa 37:24-25. A great part of this whole book of Isaiah concerneth Sennacherib.
paragraphs.anchor: For he saith.

paragraphs.text: Behold a right Pyrgopolynices, {a} whenas he was set to work by God, exalting himself both against God and man. And saith not the Pope the same when he claims to be Dominus feudi? lord paramount in spirituals and temporals; and when, in creating his cardinals, he useth these words, Estote confratres nostri, et principes mundi, Be ye fellow brethren to us and princes of the world? The Assyrian styled himself king of kings, and accounted his commanders equals to Hezekiah. {Isa 36:9} So Cardinal Bellarmine held himself King James’s mate.
paragraphs.anchor: Are not my princes altogether kings?

paragraphs.text: {a} Perhaps he had made some of his chief commanders kings. Our Henry VI crowned Henry Beauchamp, Earl of Warwick, King of the Isle of Wight.

Here in a vaunt he reckoneth up six royal cities vanquished by himself and his ancestors; and boasteth how with a wet finger, as we say, he had taken in all the country between Nineveh and Jerusalem. Of the destruction of Calno and Hamath, see Amo 6:2.
paragraphs.anchor: Is not Calno as Carchemish?

paragraphs.text: Afterwards called Antiochia.
paragraphs.anchor: Is not Hamath.

paragraphs.text: Hear how this proud braggard:
paragraphs.anchor: As Arpad?

paragraphs.text: “ Proiecit ampullas et sesquipedalia verba! ”
Have not I subdued them both pari fortitudine et felicitate?
paragraphs.anchor: Is not Samaria as Damascus?

paragraphs.text: Nota fastum tyranni, Note the arrogance of this tyrant, saith A. Lapide. It was his hand did all, and not God’s - like as afterwards Timotheus, the victorious Athenian, into whose toils cities were said to fall even as he was sleeping, telling his countrymen of his great successes, inserted ever and anon these words, Herein fortune did nothing - and then, his hand only found those kingdoms, as an obvious prey, which he did no more but meet, and it was taken.
paragraphs.anchor: As my hand hath found.

paragraphs.text: “ Dextra mihi Deus, et telum quod missile libro. ” - Virg.
In despite of their tutelary deities, which indeed were but deunculi, petty gods, as the word here used (Elil) signifieth.
paragraphs.anchor: The kingdoms of the idols.

paragraphs.text: Os ferreum! vah scelus! Prodigious blasphemy! This absurd collation and prelation of climb and dunghill idols before the true and living God is omnium mortalium execratione dignissima.
paragraphs.anchor: And whose graven images did excel them of Jerusalem.

paragraphs.text: God is not in all this man’s thoughts; himself doeth all that is done.
paragraphs.anchor: Shall I not as I have done.

paragraphs.text: Why, no; for "their rock is not as our rock," might God’s people have replied., "our enemies themselves being judges." Vere magnus est Deus Christianorum, said a certain pagan truly. The God of the Christians is a great God above all gods. But the devil doeth all he can to drive us to despair.
paragraphs.anchor: So do to Jerusalem.

paragraphs.text: Heb., And. A close connection: where pride is in the saddle, there destruction is on the crupper; {a} when the scum is at highest, it falls in the fire.
paragraphs.anchor: Wherefore.

paragraphs.text: When he hath sufficiently chastised his children by this rod of his wrath, he will cast it into the fire; {so Jer 25:1-38} when other nations have drunk deep of the cup of the divine displeasure, Babylon shall suck up the dregs. What became of the primitive persecutors, and of such as were most active here in those dogdays of Queen Mary? See the Acts and Monuments of the Church.
paragraphs.anchor: When the Lord hath performed.

paragraphs.text: For there he usually beginneth; {Jer 25:18 1Pe 4:17} his own he least of all spareth. {Amo 3:2}
paragraphs.anchor: Upon Mount Zion.

paragraphs.text: His arrogant words and lofty looks, proceeding from the pride of his heart. But let himself tell what those fruits are.
paragraphs.anchor: I will punish the fruit of the stout heart.

paragraphs.text: {a} A leathern strap buckled to the back of the saddle and passing under the horse’s tail, to prevent the saddle from slipping forwards.

Viva haec est istius Veiovis Latialis, hoc est Pontificis pictura, saith Scultetus - i.e., Here we have a lively picture of Antichrist, who speaketh great things and blasphemies, {Rev 13:5} arrogates to himself all power and wisdom, disposeth of kingdoms at his pleasure robbeth their treasures, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: For he saith, By the strength of my hand, &c.

paragraphs.text: See Isa 10:10.
paragraphs.anchor: And my hand had found.

paragraphs.text: Or, As in a nest, where a man need but only put in his hand and take out the birds or eggs, and hath none to withstand him. Thrasonica Allegoria.
paragraphs.anchor: As a nest.

paragraphs.text: Whereon they sat abrood, as it were, but I have unnested and despoiled them. They meanwhile, as silly doves, saved themselves by flight, not fight; or else, sitting in their dove cots, saw their nests destroyed, young ones taken away and killed before their eyes, never offering to rescue or revenge.
paragraphs.anchor: The riches of the people.

paragraphs.text: Is not God the architect and chief agent - the Assyrian only the instrument in his hand? What a madness, then, is it for him thus to vaunt and vapour? is the man in his right mind, think ye? How much better that victorious emperor, Charles V, who, instead of Caesar’s Veni, vidi, vici, I came, i saw, I conquered, wrote Veni, vidi, sed Christus vicit! I came, I saw, but Christ conquers, Christ is the only conqueror.
paragraphs.anchor: Shall the axe boast itself.

paragraphs.text: Or, When the rod is lift up, is it not wood, lignum inanime, sorry wood?
paragraphs.anchor: As if the staff should lift up itself.

paragraphs.text: Therefore shall the Lord … send among his fat ones,] i.e., Pingues, torosos et validos milites, his lusty and mastive soldiers, in whom he confided.
i.e., Luem, a plague to tame them, and take them down. See this fulfilled, Isa 37:36.
paragraphs.anchor: Leanness

paragraphs.text: i.e., His huge army wherein he glorieth. What need we to fear the Turks, said Sigismund, the young king of Hungary, who need not at all to fear the falling of the heavens? which, if they should fall, yet were we able with our spears and halberds to hold them up from falling upon us. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And under his glory

paragraphs.text: A plague parching up their vitals. The Hebrews say that the bodies of Sennacherib’s soldiers were, by the stroke of an angel, so consumed and burnt up, as that their garments and weapons were not burnt at all.
paragraphs.anchor: He will kindle a burning.

paragraphs.text: {a} Turkish History, fol. 206.
To Israel he shall be a comfortable light - to their enemies a consuming fire, as Exo 14:24. Ecce idem iustis et fidelibus suavis, impiis autem gravis.
paragraphs.anchor: And the light of Israel shall be for a fire.

paragraphs.text: His army, which is so troublesome and vexatious to Israel. God will "go through them, he will burn them {a} together." {Isa 27:4}
paragraphs.anchor: His thorns and his briers.

paragraphs.text: i.e., In one night, being part of the natural day. So the Spanish Armada was quickly dispersed, which had been so many years in rigging and setting forward.
paragraphs.anchor: In one day

paragraphs.text: {a} Assyrios, quibus ut sentibus vepribusque cohorrebat terra. - Jun.
i.e., Of his army, cutting his way through a wood of men, and felling the very glory of his glory, even his best soldiers. All this God shall do to his stout warriors and stately princes.
paragraphs.anchor: And he shall consume the glory of his forest

paragraphs.text: i.e., Full and whole, both here and in hell. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Both soul and body

paragraphs.text: Heb., Melteth - i.e., through fear casting away his colours: soon after which the whole regiment is routed, and cannot be rallied.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall be as when a standard-bearer fainteth.

paragraphs.text: {a} Ecce hic habes animam ardere. - Oecolamp.
And the rest of the trees … shall be few.] Heb., A number; methe mispar, a poor few, and inconsiderable company, that may soon be told.
The Hebrews say that Sennacherib escaped home with ten only in his company.
paragraphs.anchor: That a child may write them.

paragraphs.text: Meras consolationes hic loquitur Deus, {a} saith Scultetus. Here God begins to speak pure comforts to his poor people. Here he setteth forth how he will be a lively light to Israel, like as he had been a devouring fire to the Assyrians.
paragraphs.anchor: And it shall come to pass in that day.

paragraphs.text: Piscator; ictus sapiet; they had paid for their learning, smarted for their creature confidence, and now they would be better advised, viz., under Hezekiah, than they had been under Ahaz. {2Ki 16:10 Hos 14:3}
paragraphs.anchor: Shall no more again stay upon him that smote them.

paragraphs.text: {a} Scultet.
scil., To the Lord by true repentance, from whom they had deeply revolted. But of these there is but as a "remnant" - a poor few - in comparison of the whole piece of cloth.
paragraphs.anchor: A remnant shall return

paragraphs.text: i.e., Shall be saved from Sennacherib, but especially from Satan, that old man slayer. {Rom 9:27; Rom 9:29; Rom 11:5} The greater part of the Jews were then cut off by the Assyrians; and so they are spiritually still by the evil spirits which hold them in their hardness of heart, and hinder them from embracing the Christian faith. But this befalleth them by God’s holy decree {Rom 9:27-28} and just judgment.
paragraphs.anchor: Yet a remnant of them shall return

paragraphs.text: i.e., The utter destruction of this perverse people, both temporal and spiritual, {Rom 9:27} for the generality of them, is not to be accounted cruelty, but overflowing righteousness. For God could not in justice but thus rigorously deal with them; and then for his promise sake to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, reserving a "remnant," show favour to them again.
paragraphs.anchor: The consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness

paragraphs.text: Here the same thing is repeated, by way of asseveration, because not easily believed or digested, but would lie heavy as hard meat. "Behold the severity of God," {Rom 11:22} and stoop to it.
paragraphs.anchor: For the Lord God of hosts shall make, &c.

paragraphs.text: Quam paterne omnia. As a father bespeaketh his little son passing with him through a dark entry, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: O my people that dwellest in Zion, be not afraid.

paragraphs.text: Chasten thee, but not slay thee. {a} Sinite virgam corripientem, ne sentiatis malleum conterentem.
paragraphs.anchor: He shall smite thee with a rod.

paragraphs.text: Or, But he shall lift up his staff for thee, so some render it - i.e., God shall, and that "after the manner of Egypt," as of old he did for the fathers against Pharaoh.
paragraphs.anchor: And shall lift up his staff against thee.

paragraphs.text: {a} Non occidet te, quamvis vapulet. - Oecolamp.

Heb., A little little, or a little of a little. Yet a little modicum, and wrath shall be at an end. Oecolampadius rendereth it, Adhuc paululum, minus quam paululum. Hold out therefore faith and patience.
paragraphs.anchor: For yet a very little while.

paragraphs.text: Far worse than that rod. {Isa 10:24} This scourge was that angel that slew so many Assyrians in a night, according to that "slaughter of Midian." {Jdg 7:22 Psa 83:9; Psa 83:11}
paragraphs.anchor: And the Lord of hosts shall stir up a scourge for him.

paragraphs.text: Where Oreb was slain, like as was Sennacherib after this, in his temple at Nineveh.
paragraphs.anchor: At the rock of Oreb.

paragraphs.text: As Moses by his rod or staff held over the Red Sea made way for Israel, but brought destruction on the Egyptians. {Exo 14:26}
paragraphs.anchor: And as his rod was upon the sea.

paragraphs.text: That is, because or for the sake of Messiah the Prince, {Dan 9:25} the Lord Christ, our Sωτηρ and Sospitator, the foundation of all the Church’s deliverances. The whole chapter following is a comment on this sweet promise.
paragraphs.anchor: And the yoke shall be destroyed, because of the anointing.

paragraphs.text: Elegans hypotyposis, a dainty description of Sennacherib’s invasion into the land, and progress with his army toward Jerusalem, through the tribe of Benjamin.
paragraphs.anchor: He is come to Aiath.

paragraphs.text: Fourteen cities are here set down in order, as distressed by this Poliorceres, of whom it might be truly said, as it is now of the Grand Signor, that no grass groweth on that ground where he hath set his foot once,
paragraphs.anchor: He is passed to Migron.

paragraphs.text: i.e., He shall; but the prophet speaketh of it as if presently done, or as if himself had been marching along with them.
paragraphs.anchor: At Michmash he hath laid up his carriages

paragraphs.text: i.e., The straits, between two rocks. {1Sa 13:22}
paragraphs.anchor: They are gone over the passages

paragraphs.text: Heb., Hinni, i.e., claram vocem ede, eamque lugubrem, make a grievous outcry, eiula, quiritare; nam certa tibi imminet vastitas, for thou art undone.
paragraphs.anchor: Lift up thy voice.

paragraphs.text: Jeremiah’s country; "poor," because plundered.
paragraphs.anchor: O poor Anathoth.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Fled for fear, as Gibeah. {Isa 10:29}
paragraphs.anchor: Madmena is removed

paragraphs.text: viz., At Jerusalem, as threatening her destruction; but she shall shake her head at him in contempt {Isa 37:21} God oft lets his enemies go to the utmost of their tether, and then pulls them back to their tasks with shame enough, as he did Pharaoh.
paragraphs.anchor: He shall shake his hand

paragraphs.text: i.e., Those of greatest state and stature in the Assyrian army.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, the Lord shall lop the bough

paragraphs.text: See Isa 2:11; Isa 2:17.
paragraphs.anchor: And the haughty shall be humbled.

paragraphs.text: {a} That is, by an angel. {Isa 37:36 Psa 78:25; Psa 89:5-6}
paragraphs.anchor: By a mighty one.

paragraphs.text: {a} Per magnificum.
